Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of needs:
- In-product search & assistant for merchant help center (short queries mostly, plus some longer context flows)
- Hard latency SLOs for interactive UI (target p95 < 200ms for the primary flow)
- Predictable unit cost and ability to scale for seasonal spikes

Initial recommendations (model fit / eval plan):
- Recommend starting with Redwood-verified rw-medium-7b as a baseline for production evaluation (good TPS/latency tradeoff).
- Evaluate rw-large-13b for higher quality on edge cases (esp. long-context follow-ups) and compare against rw-medium using your sample prompt set.
- We can also provide quantized variants (int8) if you need lower cost with similar quality.

Resources I attached / linked below:
- Attached: acme-benchmark-summary.pdf (high-level RW-verified performance profiles for the models above)
- Attached: acme-prompt-sets.csv (sample prompt set we discussed — feel free to swap in your live queries)
- Benchmark docs: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-retail-2026

What we need from you to run the evaluation:
1) A ~500–1,000 sample queries (we can use the attached prompt set as a template)
2) Define the target conversation paths that must meet p95 latency < 200ms
3) Any data residency or PKI/KMS constraints for Private deployment testing

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- If you’re good with the plan, we’ll schedule a short 30–45m run to deploy rw-medium-7b + rw-large-13b against your sample set this week.
- We’ll share a benchmark report (TPS, p50/p95/p99 latencies, quality comparison) within 48 hours of the run.

Looping in Alex (engineering) to coordinate the benchmark run and to check capacity for a dedicated churn/throughput test.

Samir —

Short answers up front, then specifics below:
- rw-medium-7b (Redwood-verified) in us-west colocated infra: typical p95 ~75–110ms on the sample interactive flow we use in benchmarks (see numbers below). It comfortably meets your p95 < 200ms requirement.
- We include a standard quality regression harness (prompt-based evals + holdout test set) — I attached the prompt set and you can swap in your queries; we report pass/fail and similarity metrics and flag hallucination rates.

Redwood-verified performance profiles (example, measured on our us-west cluster; results are per-model medians from recent runs):
- rw-medium-7b (fp16 / int8 options): TPS (tokens/sec): 120–160; latency p50: 22–30ms; latency p95: 60–110ms; latency p99: 120–180ms.
- rw-large-13b (fp16): TPS: 45–70; latency p50: 55–85ms; latency p95: 160–220ms; latency p99: 240–320ms.

Notes and caveats:
- Latency numbers are for our benchmark prompt mix (mix of short queries + 2–3 turn contexts). If your queries skew longer or require retrieval, expect p95 to increase — retrieval adds network/DB time outside model inference.
- Quantized int8 variants typically reduce cost ~30–45% and improve TPS; p95 can slightly increase depending on kernel choices. We recommend running both fp16 and int8 for a quick quality check.
- Quality regression concerns: we run a diff against a baseline prompt set and report precision/recall on labeled items, plus a hallucination rate (false entity hallucinations per 1k responses). If you have labeled hits/misses from your production logs we can include them.

Benchmark links & artifacts:
- Public benchmark landing: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-retail-2026
- Raw run results (CSV + latency histograms): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1acme-benchmark-report
- Prompt set used in this run (attached): acme-prompt-sets.csv

Next steps:
1) Send the sanitized ~800 queries (or confirm we should use the attached sample set).
2) Alex to coordinate a 30–45m run against both rw-medium-7b and rw-large-13b (fp16 + int8 where available).
3) We’ll deliver a detailed benchmark report and a short quality regression summary within 48 hours of the run.

I’ll queue capacity now — Alex, can you confirm availability for a run later today or tomorrow morning PST?

Thanks,
Marissa
